title: R10 — What the language refuses to say

props.covers: The operation language carries concrete geometry rather than abstract align, fan, grid, or gap constraints; the aesthetic supplies relational intent, while fresh digests and renders provide the evidence used to judge it.

text.insert: R10 — What the language refuses to say

The operation surface expresses concrete entities, and every geometry edit uses a complete finite rectangle. It has no align, fan, lattice, equal-gap, or importance-size field; those meanings come from deliberate repeated geometry, section structure, labels, and color.

defines the relational vocabulary: same size plus same gap means peers, a larger box means more important, an off-register box means exception, and a parent centers over its children. The agent realizes those relations with explicit geometry: match_size carries peer size, and the exact pitch comes from the latest BOARD digest. The rectangles that result snap to the agent's 20 grid as quantization. Every successful gesture returns a result from
sized to that one operation, and a refused call carries only its error lines. A look is a framed close-up of one region — a section or object by

, one or the other and never both — while the board render itself rides the state block, so the whole picture arrives without being asked for. No diagnostic enforces abstract peer alignment or equal-gap intent: the always-on diagnostics guard physical readability, and the renders remain the composition judge.
